unit.title: Number Systems, Factors & Estimation
unit.essential_question: How does number structure help us calculate efficiently, recognize patterns, and judge whether results make sense?
big_ideas: Number sets are nested and connected.
Factors and prime structure describe how whole numbers are built.
Shared factors and multiples solve grouping and synchronization problems.
The order of operations preserves shared mathematical meaning.
Estimation is a reasoning tool, not merely rough arithmetic.
unit.architecture: Open-age foundational Pre-Algebra entry unit: number systems + factors/multiples + prime/divisibility structure + GCF/LCM + order of operations + estimation/reasonableness + mastery
unit.readiness_note: Unit 01 is intentionally a six-lesson foundation and evidence-gathering unit. It establishes prerequisite number sense before the Unit 02 readiness/pathway bridge; advancement is based on demonstrated mastery, not age or grade identity.

lessons.title: Number Families & the Real Number System
objectives: Classify natural, whole, integer, rational, irrational, and real numbers.
Explain how the major real-number sets are nested inside one another.
Represent, compare, and order rational and irrational values on a number line.
Identify the most specific number set that contains a value.
Justify a classification using fractions, decimal behavior, or perfect-square reasoning.

lessons.title: Factors, Multiples & Number Structure
objectives: List all positive factor pairs of a whole number systematically.
Generate multiples and identify common multiples.
Distinguish clearly between factors and multiples.
Use arrays, rectangles, and equal-group models to represent factor relationships.
Explain how perfect squares affect the number of positive factors.

lessons.title: Prime Numbers, Divisibility & Prime Factorization
objectives: Classify whole numbers greater than 1 as prime or composite.
Apply divisibility rules for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, and 10.
Write composite numbers as products of prime factors.
Use factor trees and repeated division to verify prime factorizations.
Explain why prime factorization is unique apart from factor order.

lessons.title: Greatest Common Factor & Least Common Multiple
objectives: Find the greatest common factor of two or more whole numbers.
Find the least common multiple of two or more whole numbers.
Use factor lists and prime factorizations to determine GCF and LCM.
Distinguish situations that require a GCF from situations that require an LCM.
Explain solutions to grouping and synchronization problems using mathematical evidence.

lessons.title: Order of Operations & Evaluating Expressions
objectives: Evaluate numerical expressions using grouping symbols, exponents, multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction.
Explain why multiplication and division are performed from left to right when they share a level of priority.
Explain why addition and subtraction are performed from left to right when they share a level of priority.
Use substitution and the order of operations to evaluate simple variable expressions.
Identify and correct common order-of-operations errors.

lessons.title: Estimation, Compatible Numbers & Reasonableness
objectives: Estimate sums, differences, products, and quotients using purposeful rounding.
Use compatible numbers and front-end estimation for efficient mental calculation.
Choose an estimation strategy appropriate to the numbers and context.
Use estimates, magnitude, and operation sense to judge whether exact results are reasonable.
Explain when an exact answer is necessary and when an estimate is more useful.

practice.title: Foundation Practice
practice.description: 20-question scaffolded review with optional hints and smaller steps.

practice.title: Core Practice
practice.description: 20-question complete unit-level rehearsal across all six lessons.
